opening.text: It's lunchtime at a new school. You stand with your tray and look around. Every table seems full. Every group seems to know each other. For a long minute, you wonder if there is a seat for you. Then someone waves and slides over. "Sit here." Few words matter more than that.

mainMessage.text: Everyone needs a seat at the table. God has one saved for each of us, and we can save one for others.

blocks.text: **Many feel alone** Loneliness is real, and it is common. If you feel it, you aren't strange. Many do.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “No One Sits Alone” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Today many feel lonely and isolated.
Many feel alone.
**We need to belong** Belonging isn't a luxury. It's something we need to be well.
That there should be no schism in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Doctrine of Belonging” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
A sense of belonging is important to our physical, mental, and spiritual well-being.
Belonging matters.
**The Savior counts us** No matter how we feel, the Savior knows our name and our place. He counts each of us.

What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it? And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
Elder David L. Buckner, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Ye Are My Friends” from the October 2024 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
The sentiment is clear: the Savior numbers each of us and watches over us.
He counts you.
**Don't wait to be invited** Sometimes we sit and wait to be asked. Belonging often starts when we reach out.
And let every man esteem his brother as himself, and practice virtue and holiness before me.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Doctrine of Belonging” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Belonging comes not as we wait for it but as we reach out to help one another.
Reach out.
**Be the one who waves** We can be the person who slides over and says, "Sit here." That small act changes a day.
Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “No One Sits Alone” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
In His restored Church, we are all better when no one sits alone.
Save a seat.
**We need each other, and we need Him** A table works best when we are all at it. We come together to worship, and He is there.
For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
Elder David L. Buckner, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Ye Are My Friends” from the October 2024 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
I worship on Sunday as a reminder that we need each other and together we need Him.
Come to the table.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone made room for them, or when they made room for someone. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Elijah feels alone

blocks.text: Elijah ran into the wilderness. He felt that he was the only faithful one left.

And he said, I have been very jealous for the Lord God of hosts: for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away. And after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice. Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him.
Elijah believed he was alone. He wasn't. The Lord spoke to him gently and told him there were thousands who were faithful too.

application.text: First, think of one person who may feel left out in your ward or branch. Second, pray for the courage to say hello. Third, sit with them next Sunday.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the Savior counts each of us. I know there is a seat for everyone at His table. I know small acts of welcome change lives. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

versions.analogy: A seat at the lunch table

opening.text: A family moves to a new town. The boxes are everywhere. The streets are strange. No one knows their name. The first week feels very long. Then a neighbor knocks with a plate of food and says, "Welcome. We're glad you're here." The town feels a little smaller and a little warmer. That is what belonging does.

mainMessage.text: Belonging often begins with one neighbor who knocks on the door.

blocks.text: **The new-town ache** Moving, changing jobs, losing a friend, or growing older can leave us feeling alone. Many carry that ache.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “No One Sits Alone” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Today many feel lonely and isolated.
The ache is common.
**A home is more than a house** A house becomes a home when we feel we belong. We need that for our whole well-being.
That there should be no schism in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Doctrine of Belonging” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
A sense of belonging is important to our physical, mental, and spiritual well-being.
Home means belonging.
**The Savior knows the address** The Savior knows where we live and what we're carrying. He watches over each of us.

What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it? And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
Elder David L. Buckner, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Ye Are My Friends” from the October 2024 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
The sentiment is clear: the Savior numbers each of us and watches over us.
He knows where you are.
**Knock first** The new family waits. The neighbors knock. Belonging grows as we reach out.
And let every man esteem his brother as himself, and practice virtue and holiness before me.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Doctrine of Belonging” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Belonging comes not as we wait for it but as we reach out to help one another.
Knock first.
**No stranger at the table** In the Church, no one should sit alone. We are not strangers. We are one household.
Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “No One Sits Alone” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
In His restored Church, we are all better when no one sits alone.
No strangers here.
**A neighborhood needs neighbors** We can't be a neighborhood by ourselves. We gather to worship, and we find Him and each other.
For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
Elder David L. Buckner, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Ye Are My Friends” from the October 2024 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
I worship on Sunday as a reminder that we need each other and together we need Him.
We need each other.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they were new somewhere and were welcomed. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Ruth, the stranger

blocks.text: Ruth was a stranger in a foreign land. She went to the fields to find food. Boaz noticed her.

Then she fell on her face, and bowed herself to the ground, and said unto him, Why have I found grace in thine eyes, that thou shouldest take knowledge of me, seeing I am a stranger? The Lord recompense thy work, and a full reward be given thee of the Lord God of Israel, under whose wings thou art come to trust.
Ruth felt like a stranger. Boaz made her feel she belonged. One kind act began her new life.

application.text: First, think of someone new in your ward, branch or neighborhood. Second, ask Heavenly Father how to welcome them. Third, knock, call, or send a note this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the Lord knows us when we are new and alone. I know welcome can change a whole season. I know no one has to be a stranger. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: At a big gathering, you get a name tag. At first, it feels like a small thing. But something changes when someone looks at it and says your name. "Hi, Sarah." Suddenly you are not just a face in the crowd. You are known. Loneliness often begins to ease when we are called by name.

mainMessage.text: Loneliness eases when we are known by name. God knows ours.

blocks.text: **The crowd and the ache** We can stand in a crowded room and feel completely alone. Many do.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “No One Sits Alone” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Today many feel lonely and isolated.
The ache is real.
**Being known matters** Being known is part of being well. We need it for our hearts and our faith.
That there should be no schism in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Doctrine of Belonging” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
A sense of belonging is important to our physical, mental, and spiritual well-being.
Being known matters.
**He knows your name** The Savior doesn't see a crowd. He sees each person. He counts each one.

What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it? And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
Elder David L. Buckner, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Ye Are My Friends” from the October 2024 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
The sentiment is clear: the Savior numbers each of us and watches over us.
He knows your name.
**Say the first hello** Waiting for someone to say our name can take a long time. Often we begin by saying theirs.
And let every man esteem his brother as himself, and practice virtue and holiness before me.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Doctrine of Belonging” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Belonging comes not as we wait for it but as we reach out to help one another.
Say their name.
**No one left with a blank tag** In His Church, no one should sit alone and unnoticed. We are one household.
Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “No One Sits Alone” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
In His restored Church, we are all better when no one sits alone.
Notice each one.
**Gathered together** A name tag means more in a room of people. We gather to worship, and we find that we need each other, and Him.
For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
Elder David L. Buckner, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Ye Are My Friends” from the October 2024 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
I worship on Sunday as a reminder that we need each other and together we need Him.
Gather together.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone remembered their name and it mattered. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Hagar in the wilderness

blocks.text: Hagar was alone in the desert with her son. She thought no one saw them.

And God heard the voice of the lad; and the angel of God called to Hagar out of heaven, and said unto her, What aileth thee, Hagar? fear not; for God hath heard the voice of the lad where he is. And God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water; and she went, and filled the bottle with water, and gave the lad drink.
God called her by name. He had heard. Even in the wilderness, she was known.

application.text: First, learn the name of one person at church you don't yet know. Second, say it to them with a smile. Third, remember it next week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God knows my name. I know He hears us in the wilderness. I know we can help others feel known. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: The photographer says, "Squeeze in, everyone." And people shuffle over. Someone at the edge steps in. A small child is lifted to the front. One person always stays at the back, half out of the frame. Then someone says, "Come here, we've got room." That moment of making space is what belonging looks like.

mainMessage.text: Belonging is making room in the frame, so no one stands outside it.

blocks.text: **Someone is always at the edge** In most groups, someone stands at the edge. Many feel left out and alone.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “No One Sits Alone” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Today many feel lonely and isolated.
Someone is at the edge.
**A group needs everyone in it** A photo with a gap feels incomplete. Belonging is important for all of us.
That there should be no schism in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Doctrine of Belonging” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
A sense of belonging is important to our physical, mental, and spiritual well-being.
The group needs you.
**He holds a place for you** The Savior sees the person at the edge. He counts each person and watches over each one.

What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it? And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
Elder David L. Buckner, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Ye Are My Friends” from the October 2024 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
The sentiment is clear: the Savior numbers each of us and watches over us.
He saves a place.
**Step toward the frame** If we stand at the edge, we can step in. If we are in the frame, we can reach out a hand.
And let every man esteem his brother as himself, and practice virtue and holiness before me.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Doctrine of Belonging” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Belonging comes not as we wait for it but as we reach out to help one another.
Step in. Reach out.
**Everyone in the picture** In the Church, we want everyone in the picture. No one should sit alone.
Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “No One Sits Alone” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
In His restored Church, we are all better when no one sits alone.
Make room.
**The picture is better together** A photo of one person is just a portrait. A group photo tells a story. We need each other, and we need Him.
For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
Elder David L. Buckner, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Ye Are My Friends” from the October 2024 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
I worship on Sunday as a reminder that we need each other and together we need Him.
Better together.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone made room for them in a group. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Zacchaeus in the tree

blocks.text: Zacchaeus was the chief among the tax collectors. Many in the town looked down on him. He wanted to see Jesus, but he was short and the crowd was thick.

And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature. And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zacchæus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house. And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.
Jesus stopped in the crowd. He looked up. He called Zacchaeus by name and made room at his table. Zacchaeus received Him joyfully.

application.text: First, notice who stands at the edge of a group you are in. Second, pray for the courage to bring them in. Third, say, "Come join us," this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the Savior looks up and sees us. I know He makes room. I know we can do the same for others. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A lighthouse stands alone on a rocky point. Night after night, it sends its beam over the dark water. It may look lonely. But ships all along the coast are steering by it. The keeper is never as alone as it seems. Many are watching and counting on him. Feeling alone and being alone are not always the same thing.

mainMessage.text: Feeling alone is not the same as being alone. The Lord and others are nearer than we think.

blocks.text: **The lonely light** A lighthouse can look lonely. So can we. Many people feel this way.
And the Lord God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “No One Sits Alone” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Today many feel lonely and isolated.
Many feel lonely.
**Even a lighthouse needs a harbor** We aren't made to stand alone. Belonging helps us shine, and it keeps us well.
That there should be no schism in the body; but that the members should have the same care one for another.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Doctrine of Belonging” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
A sense of belonging is important to our physical, mental, and spiritual well-being.
We need a harbor.
**The Keeper of the Keeper** Someone watches over the lighthouse keeper. The Savior watches over each of us.

What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it? And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
Elder David L. Buckner, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Ye Are My Friends” from the October 2024 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
The sentiment is clear: the Savior numbers each of us and watches over us.
He watches over you.
**Send a signal** The lighthouse sends a beam. We can send a signal too. A call, a visit, or a kind word.
And let every man esteem his brother as himself, and practice virtue and holiness before me.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Doctrine of Belonging” from the October 2022 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
Belonging comes not as we wait for it but as we reach out to help one another.
Send a signal.
**A whole coastline of lights** Many lighthouses line the coast. Each one helps the others find the way. In His Church, no one should sit alone.
Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
Elder Gerrit W. Gong of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “No One Sits Alone” from the October 2025 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
In His restored Church, we are all better when no one sits alone.
A coast of lights.
**Ships need lights, and lights need ships** The lighthouse has a purpose because ships need it. We find our purpose with others, and with Him.
For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
Elder David L. Buckner, of the Seventy, said this in his talk “Ye Are My Friends” from the October 2024 general conference (Saturday Afternoon Session).
I worship on Sunday as a reminder that we need each other and together we need Him.
We need each other.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they felt alone but later learned they were not. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Paul stands alone

blocks.text: Paul was in prison and about to face a trial. His friends were gone.

At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge. Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
No one stood with Paul. But the Lord did. When we feel alone, His nearness can still be real.

application.text: First, think of a time you felt alone and noticed later that God was near. Second, thank Heavenly Father for it. Third, be a light to someone who feels alone this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the Lord stands with us when others do not. I know He counts each one of us. I know we can be lights for one another. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
